question.text: IRR (Internal Rate of Return) in the AIF context is preferred over simple return metrics because:

answer.text: It is always higher than simple returns
It accounts for the timing and size of cash flows (capital calls and distributions)

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes IRR/FIRR as a return measure that considers the time value of money and the uncertain, uneven cash flows of AIFs — capital drawdowns over time, distributions during the fund's life and at winding up. Because AIF cash flows are irregular, IRR gives a time-adjusted return that reflects the actual investor experience better than simple averages. The Trap: The workbook also cautions that FIRR alone is not sufficient and should be evaluated together with multiples such as TVPI/MOIC, because two funds with similar IRRs can produce very different total value creation depending on size and timing of cash flows. Note: Per the workbook, IRR (or FIRR) should always be read alongside multiples such as TVPI/MOIC. Two funds with the same IRR can deliver very different total value creation depending on the timing and size of distributions.
